newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: The rand ended steady on Tuesday after comments by Finance Minister Trevor Manuel on exchange controls and the International Monetary Fund (IMF) failed to instil confidence in the market.
It ended the day unchanged from its previous close at 4.6950/7000 on the dollar after a morning low of a 4.7040 bid.

Foreign exchange dealers said the rand held in a 4.6960 to 4.7050 range during the morning as mild importer demand was matched by a trickle of dollars out of London and players awaited a media briefing by Manuel in Cape Town.

The rand spiked weaker to above the 4.70 level on comments by Manuel that the government was currently not in discussions with the International Monetary Fund and his cautious comments on the lifting of exchange controls.
"The rand spiked weaker although not by that much much...Manuel's comments on the IMF were not received well," a forex trader said.
Another trader said market jitters were fuelled last Friday by rumours of more aggressive moves on foreign exchange control easing, backed by an IMF loan and/or interest rate hike.

"Players were nervous that something more aggressive would come out of the meeting and started buying rand last Friday but the market read Manuel's comments today (Tuesday) as 'business as usual'," said a trader at a foreign investment bank.
Another said: "The market is looking for concrete steps. Manuel's comments did not instil any confidence."

Dealers expected the currency to depreciate over the next couple of days as offshore players sold rand back into the market. Some said the rand had the potential to weaken back up to 4.75 on the dollar.
The Reserve Bank was seen in the market on the topside, eager to hold the rand below the 4.71 level, dealers said.
Against the crosses, the rand reached a new low against sterling and was last quoted at 7.7538/7668 from 7.6878/7007 overnight and at 0.3218/3222 marks from 0.3218/3223 marks previously.
Bonds ended firmer on late buying out of London after a steady performance on the day.
At 1408 GMT the key R150 was quoted at 15.89 percent from 15.92 percent at the close on Monday.
The yield on the benchmark R150 stock dipped below 15.90 percent after a better-than-expected September producer price index number and despite October new car sales coming in at a 14 year high.
"The car sales figure was shocking but the market managed to say below 15.90 percent -- which was seen as a big break -- for a while," a bond dealer said.
The yield then ticked higher above the figure in line with the rand after Manuel spoke but managed to recoup losses at the close.

Traders did not expect much activity until Thursday's bond options' close out when volatility could heighten but would be keeping an eye on U.S. Treasuries after the release of results of the U.S. presidential election early on Wednesday.
The Bond Exchange said foreigners bought a net 38.83 million rand of South African bonds on Monday after buying 24.88 million rand of bonds on Friday.
Nominal cumulative volumes stood at 3.37 billion rand on Monday from 7.78 billion rand on Friday.

On the money market, three-month NCD rates were slightly higher at between 16.40 to 16.55 percent from 16.40 to 16.50 percent, while the 90-day BA rate was slightly higher at between 15.75 to 15.90 percent from 15.75 and 15.85 percent.
The Reserve Bank indicated the daily shortage at 9.265 billion rand on Monday from 8.744 billion rand on Saturday.
-- Vera von Lieres, Johannesburg newsroom +27 11 482 1003
